strategy.summary: Reproduce cvxpy#3338 by running the project’s NLP-solver test suite on the COPT-enabled revision (buggy: a918e45f6831). The failing transition is driven by the NLP derivative checker tolerance change and the pinned evaluation point logic that prevent spurious failures; additionally, this CI job ensures the COPT optional dependency is installed (so the special_value/int-bound overflow path can execute when the COPT NLP interface constructs bounds containing the 1e30 infinity sentinel).

pip_packages: cvxpy (editable, from repo at both buggy and fixed revisions)
unopy (installed only for UNO workflow as configured; for this reproduction focus on COPT job installing .[COPT])
system_packages: Fortran compiler on macOS (CI notes it is required for macOS optional-solvers build). For Linux, not explicitly required in provided evidence.
build_commands: From repo at buggy commit a918e45f6831: create venv, install cvxpy in editable mode with testing extras; install COPT extra; then run the specific NLP solver test (below).
Use the same commands for the fixed revision from PR #3338 (not provided in the evidence as a commit hash).
pinned_because: coptpy is constrained explicitly to >=8.0.3 because the NLP callback API (NlpCallbackBase, loadNlData) only exists in coptpy >= 8.0.3; the overflow occurs in the COPT NLP interface when it assigns COPT’s float infinity sentinel (~1e30) into integer bounds.

Clarabel/OSQP/SCS/NumPy/SciPy/highspy/sparsediffpy are pinned >= documented minima since the repo CI installs all optional solvers; while the specific bug is COPT-bound typing, running the same test job avoids missing solver dispatch paths.

strategy.test_command: uv run pytest -q cvxpy/tests/nlp_tests -k "copt or COPT"
strategy.reproducing_test: cvxpy/tests/nlp_tests (COPT NLP solver path exercised by CI installation of .[COPT]); specifically, the tests that invoke cvxpy.tests.nlp_tests.derivative_checker.DerivativeChecker.check_gradient/check_hessian and therefore depend on the patched logic (pinned eval point + epsilon=1e-6).
strategy.success_criterion: On revision a918e45f6831 (buggy), the relevant NLP test(s) fail (assertion mismatch) due to the buggy behavior being reachable in the COPT NLP interface and/or the derivative checker running with the older evaluation-point inheritance and smaller epsilon (1e-8), producing a failure; on the fixed revision from PR #3338, the same pytest invocation passes because (1) the COPT interface is exercised with bounds correctly handled via the fix in PR #3338 (float-typed bounds so the 1e30 sentinel is not written into int64 bounds), and (2) the derivative checker uses epsilon=1e-6 and pins the evaluation point before computing Hessian values, eliminating spurious failures.
strategy.numerical_probe: No separate numerical value checks are required. The test oracle is the unit test’s pass/fail assertion on gradient/Hessian/solver outputs produced by the NLP solver pipeline.

input_output_examples.input: (No benchmark IO provided in the evidence; reproduce by running the pytest command above under both revisions.)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Test failure on buggy revision (assertion in derivative checker or downstream solver wrapper).
input_output_examples.expected_output: All targeted tests pass on fixed revision.

risks: The evidence does not provide the exact fixed commit hash for PR #3338; you must checkout the PR’s merged commit (or the commit that includes the bounds-typing fix) to get the passing transition.

Platform/toolchain risk: the provided CI evidence mentions a Fortran compiler for macOS optional-solvers builds. If running on macOS, ensure Fortran is installed; otherwise builds may fail and you won’t reach the solver tests.
Architecture/solver availability risk: COPT must be installed and functional via coptpy>=8.0.3; if COPT is unavailable (license/runtime), the failing path may not execute, preventing the transition.

The “special_value” overflow path depends on a variable whose only bound comes from sign/boolean attribute branches that narrow with integer literals (e.g., max(lb_val, 0) / min(ub_val, 1)), producing int64 bounds arrays from Leaf.get_bounds(). The specific test that triggers this is not named in the evidence; the strategy relies on the project’s NLP test suite selecting such a model under the COPT NLP interface.

The reproduction may also be sensitive to derivative checker behavior: the evidence shows epsilon changed from 1e-8 to 1e-6 and Hessian evaluation point pinned. If the PR-only change for float bounds happens without altering derivative checker, you may still see failures that are not caused by the special_value bug; conversely, if you only observe failures fixed by the derivative checker, you may not be validating the int-overflow root cause.

oracle.why: The evidence does not include a specific assertion or numeric threshold for the special_value failure. The only concrete oracle details in the evidence are derivative_checker.check_gradient’s epsilon change (1e-6 vs 1e-8) and tolerance adjustments in one COPT exponential-cone test (FeasTol/DualTol=1e-9). For this reproduction strategy, the pass/fail is the unit test assertions in cvxpy/tests/nlp_tests under COPT.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: pytest -q cvxpy/tests/nlp_tests -k "copt or COPT" fails on a918e45f6831 (likely via derivative checker mismatch and/or COPT NLP interface producing incorrect results due to writing the 1e30 float infinity sentinel into int64 bounds).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The same pytest invocation passes on the PR #3338 fixed revision because bounds are kept float-typed so the infinity sentinel does not corrupt integer bounds, and because derivative_checker uses epsilon=1e-6 and pins the Hessian evaluation point before computing values.
